parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Maple Ridge · Albion and Kanaka Creek
The name Albion is an MLS® sub-area label, and the City of Maple Ridge has no published boundary for it. On the City’s neighbourhoods page, the area is grouped as Albion/Kanaka.

The closest official description is the Albion Area Plan, Chapter 10.2 of the Official Community Plan, which includes the North East Albion area. The City’s planning documents also cover the Albion Flats, about 133 hectares next to the Lougheed Highway and 240th Street.
The City’s neighbourhoods page says the Albion Fairgrounds and the Albion Sport Complex, home to Planet Ice and the Golden Ears Winter Club, are here.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 17, 2026. I have worked in Lower Mainland real estate for 11+ years. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Maple Ridge and School District 42.
General information only.

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Albion

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.
The Albion Area Plan is Chapter 10.2 of the Official Community Plan. It was first adopted on July 4, 2006 and the City adopted updates on October 28, 2025.
The October 2025 update adds walking and cycling connections, supports local commercial nodes and introduces buffers where urban development meets farmland.
The plan divides North East Albion into four precincts: north of 112 Avenue, east of Lockwood Street, between 248 Street and Lockwood Street, and west of 248 Street.

The City’s targeted review of North East Albion looked at the lands south of 110 Avenue. The recommended concept includes a moderate increase in density, with townhouses along 248 Street and between 248 Street and 249 Street.

In 2025 the City adopted updates to its Official Community Plan and to the area plans for Town Centre, Hammond, Silver Valley and Albion, according to the City. The Albion update was adopted on October 28, and the rest were adopted in November.

ALR: the City’s 2015 Albion Flats update report says most of the Albion Flats is in the Agricultural Land Reserve and outside the City’s Urban Area Boundary. The exceptions are generally along 240th Street south of 104th Avenue, where there is housing, Albion Elementary and the historic commercial node where Bruce’s Market is located.
The report puts the Albion Flats at about 133 hectares (329 acres) in south-central Maple Ridge, next to the Lougheed Highway and 240th Street.

Flood: the City’s Official Community Plan (section 6.2.3), as quoted in the 2015 report, says the Albion Flats is within the floodplain of the Fraser River and is associated with high ecological value.

Properties close to the Fraser River floodplain get the City’s Be Flood Ready guide in the mail. Inside is a floodplain map for the Fraser River along with a summary of how the City would respond to a flood.
According to the City, flood risk is handled case by case. A Floodplain Management Bylaw has been proposed, and it would bring clearer rules such as minimum building elevations.
I did not find a City slope or ravine statement for the Albion residential area, or a published flood construction level for it. Ask the City about floodplain and creek rules for the exact lot.
Transit: Albion has no West Coast Express station. The nearest is Port Haney Station at 22300 River Road.

The proposed Langley–Haney Place Bus Rapid Transit line from TransLink would cover 22 km, with 13 stations and a bus every 10 minutes at peak. TransLink describes it as being in detailed planning, with preliminary funding from the 2025 Investment Plan and more funding still needed to build it.
